title: Succession Infrastructure Plan™
intro: Make sure what you built can continue without you, through The IV Phases™: what must continue, what depends on you, how it is carried day to day, and how it is handed on.

nodes.prompt: What have you built that must continue if you step away, and why does it matter to the people it serves?
Which values and standards should the next leader keep, even if everything else changes?

nodes.section: Phase II — What depends on you
nodes.prompt: Imagine you are unreachable for thirty days. Which decisions, relationships and systems would stop moving?

nodes.section: Phase II — What depends on you
nodes.prompt: Which key decisions and their reasoning are written down, and which live only in your head?

nodes.section: Phase II — What depends on you
nodes.prompt: Who could explain your priorities in your absence today, and who should be able to?

nodes.section: Phase III — How it is carried day to day
nodes.prompt: Which important documents, accounts and systems can only you open, and who else should have access?

nodes.section: Phase III — How it is carried day to day
nodes.prompt: Which critical relationships (partners, clients, funders, community) need a second person who knows them?

nodes.section: Phase III — How it is carried day to day
nodes.prompt: What regular practice will move knowledge out of informal conversation and into writing?
Who could carry this work forward: a successor, a team member, an apprentice, or a partner organization?
What would they need from you first, and how will you bring them up to speed?
What happens to unfinished work if you step away tomorrow?
When will you review this plan again, and who will hold you to it?

closing.prompt: The one piece of this work I will hand on or write down first, to whom, and by when:
